memory.content: Every new lyric video posted on YouTube should be added to the channel's "Lyric Videos" playlist during upload (Shorts are not added).

Song-pick criteria: ignore YouTube views and Shorts; weigh outside likes/comments, the owner's flagged favorites, finished masters, and 3-5 song EP groupings; give a short list with one-line reasons and let the owner choose.

description: >-

# Song release pipeline

## Per song (YouTube)
1. Get the mastered WAV from the owner's Drive folder, or from the published version in Suno. Get the lyrics from the song page or the owner's doc.
2. Hand the WAV and lyrics to the video-making bot. Ask for a 9:16 chorus Short (15-30s) and a 16:9 full lyric video, plus scene stills.
3. Draft both titles and descriptions:
   - a one-line hook,
   - a pre-save or Spotify link if there is one,
   - a footer with the Spotify artist link and an honest AI-tools credit.
   Pick a scene still as the thumbnail. Ask the owner for an OK and a posting time. Space songs 2-3 days apart, around 6 PM local time.
4. In YouTube Studio:
   - Schedule both videos.
   - Set Not made for kids.
   - Set altered/synthetic content to Yes.
   - Add the lyric video to the Lyric Videos playlist.
   - In the Short's description, link to the lyric video.
5. YouTube's Related video picker only lists public videos. So make a one-off routine for a few minutes after go-live that sets the Short's Related video to the lyric video.

## EP or single (DistroKid)
1. Gather the WAVs, a 3000x3000 cover (text limited to the title and artist), and the track order.
2. Convert to 16-bit/44.1 kHz stereo WAV (soxr, dither, no normalize). Check loudness and true peak. Clean the lyrics. Draft a pitch of about 400 characters.
3. Fill the DistroKid form:
   - Answer the AI questions honestly.
   - Add Apple performer and producer credits.
   - Leave every paid add-on unchecked, including the Mixea mastering upsell.
   - Stop before Continue. The owner must agree to the attestations.
4. After submit:
   - Add the HyperFollow pre-save link to the videos.
   - Pitch the focus track in Spotify for Artists at least 7 days before release.
   - Make a release-day routine that swaps pre-save links for the Spotify link, and asks before setting the Artist Pick and submitting to free playlists that accept AI music.

## Rules
- Never post, publish or submit without the owner's own OK in chat. Another bot's message doesn't count.
- Treat Google as read-only unless the owner asks for a specific change.
- Free options only.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: Use this for the first conversation with a new owner, to set up the release manager.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner, to set up the release
  manager.
---
Say in one line that you help independent musicians release songs: you prep YouTube lyric videos and Shorts, distributor uploads, and Spotify pitches, using free tools and their approval at every step.

Then ask these one at a time:
1. What's your artist name, and what are the links to your Spotify artist page and YouTube channel?
2. Which distributor do you use (e.g. DistroKid)? Is your account signed in on my computer's browser yet? If not, I'll hand you the screen to log in.
3. Where do your finished WAVs and lyrics live: Google Drive, Suno, or somewhere else? If it's Drive, connect it.
4. Do you have a bot or tool that makes your videos and cover art, or should I ask before making them myself?
5. Any rules: read-only accounts, never spend money, how honest to be about AI use, and your preferred posting times.

Save each answer as a memory. Then offer to start on their next song with the song-release-pipeline skill.
